newsitem.title: GERMANY: Karstadt says CEO rumours unfounded.
newsitem.headline: Karstadt says CEO rumours unfounded.

text.p: German retailer Karstadt AG said on Wednesday media speculation about a chief executive change was unfounded.

"The public discussion about personalities at the top of Karstadt AG has brought unrest to the company," the firm said in a statement. "To end it, the supervisory board clearly states that the various speculation about a new chief executive is totally lacking in any foundation."
Karstadt last week postponed a supervisory board meeting after financial publications had speculated that chief Walter Deuss would be forced to step down.
The company has not yet announced a new date for the meeting, which had been originally scheduled for March 22.

The news reports said Karstadt stores lost 300 million marks last year, a figure the company has not confirmed. They also said Karstadt's main shareholders -- the Hertie foundation, Deutsche Bank AG and Commerzbank AG -- sought Deuss's removal.

In its statement on Wednesday, Karstadt said: "The chosen new direction of Karstadt is intended to be brought forward quickly. To reach our goals, the management board, with its chief, Walter Deuss, is charged with bringing the required measures into operation."
